question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool scheduling mode, and must it wait for explicit tool concurrency-safety metadata before any early execution is allowed?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix changes core runtime semantics and safety policy rather than repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open for an owner design covering scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, provider differences, and regression proof.

options.title: Block On Tool Safety Metadata
options.body: Treat early execution as dependent on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract.

options.title: Defer Runtime Semantics Change
options.body: Keep current post-stream batching as the only supported behavior if maintainers decide the latency win is not worth the safety and compatibility risk.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for an owner design covering scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, provider differences, and regression proof.
